defects.claim: Unit places above 100 make toDisplay call toFixed with an out-of-range argument and throw RangeError
defects.scenario: A linear unit with scale 1 and places 101, which the schema editor's Unit places control accepts; toDisplay calls toFixed(101) and throws RangeError, so the field cannot render
defects.cause: places not clamped to the formatter limit

defects.claim: A custom suffix colliding with a system unit's suffix is remapped to that unit's factor, so a round trip reads back at the wrong magnitude
defects.scenario: A metric unit displaying centimeters with custom suffix mm: the accepted-suffix mapping gives mm factor 1, then the loop replaces it with the millimeter-to-centimeter factor 0.1, so a formatted value reads back at a tenth of its magnitude
defects.cause: suffix map lets system units override the custom suffix

defects.claim: An owner's switch inside a section is never spared, so the owner can never be turned back on
defects.scenario: an `object` leaf `stroke` with `enableIf: { path: 'stroke.on' }`, whose field `on` sits under a section `edge` in `children` (a section adds nothing to the path, so `stroke.on` is directly a field of `stroke`). With `on` false: `stroke` is disabled and its owner `disablesOwn`. `members` calls `section(child, …, owner.status, …, owner.switchOf)`; the section's status is `prefStatusUnder(owner.status, …)` = disabled, and the section's own owner has `above.enabled === false`, so `disablesOwn` is false and `switchReads` is never asked about `stroke.on`. `on` comes out disabled with everything else, so the switch can never be flipped back on. The same holds for a section schema root, or any section, whose `enableIf` reads a member of a nested section. It should be spared the way a field sitting directly in `children` is. `statusMatching` in statusAt.ts:173 builds the section owner the same way, so `prefStatusAt` gives the same wrong answer.
defects.cause: section owner drops the enclosing owner's switch (switchOf only passed through, never set to the disabling owner)

defects.claim: prefAliasedLeaf draws the target's disabledReason and hidden in place of the alias's own
defects.scenario: an alias with its own `disabledReason: 'Turn on Snap first'` (it has its own `enableIf`, which status.ts honors) is drawn through `prefAliasedLeaf` by routing's `resolveMenu` and prefs' `aliasTargets`/`edit/aliases`. `...rest` is the target's fields, and the alias contributes only name/description/short/access/pair/heading/tags. So the tooltip shows the target's reason (or none), and a target marked `hidden` (shown on purpose only through an alias elsewhere) makes the drawn leaf `hidden: true`. The alias's own presentational fields should win where it gives them, as its name does.
defects.cause: alias's own PrefBase fields not overlaid

defects.claim: A root-path condition into a list or map entry compares the stored form, not the shown one
defects.scenario: a list `styles` whose item is an object with a boolean field `italic` carrying an `encoding` (stores `'italic'`). The condition `{ path: 'styles.0.italic', is: true }` is judged by `prefJudge`. `prefReader` reads through the item (`fieldValue` → `entryAt`), but `prefShownReader` asks `prefLeavesHolding`, which returns `UNSEEN` for any path into a `list`/`map`, so the value is never decoded and `'italic' === true` fails. Two pathways answer "which leaf describes this value" differently: the reader knows the item, the decoder does not. `insideLeaf` should descend into `item` for an entry step, as `prefLeavesHoldingIn` does for `from: 'item'`.
defects.cause: list/map treated as unseen though `item` describes entries

defects.claim: repairPrefValue throws on a list or map leaf with no item, which status.ts says an app's leaf may have
defects.scenario: an app draws its own leaf under the built-in kind `list` (or `map`) with no `item`. status.ts:117 handles exactly this ("A leaf an app's renderer draws under a built-in's kind may hold no item"), and so do judge.ts `entryAt`, helpers.ts `visibleInside` and statusAt.ts `statusInside`. When a non-empty array (or object) is stored for that leaf, `repairList` maps each entry through `repairPrefValue(leaf.item, …)` with `leaf.item === undefined`. `leaf.kind` then throws a TypeError, so reading the stored value fails. It should pass the entries through unrepaired, or treat the leaf as an app-defined kind.
defects.cause: missing `item === undefined` guard, answered differently from the other walks

defects.claim: A condition treats any scope-shaped value as a split value, even on a leaf with no scopes
defects.scenario: a `map` leaf (keys nobody declared) holds `{ $by: 'mode', $in: { a: 1 } }`, two keys a person can type, or an `object` / app-defined leaf has fields `$by` (a string) and `$in` (an object). `isPrefScope(value)` is true, `prefScopesOf(leaf)` is empty, so the selection is empty and `prefScopeValue` returns the scope's `$else`, else `leaf.default`. A condition on that leaf (`{ path: 'tags' }`, `isSet`) then compares the default rather than the value stored: it reads "not set" while the map holds two keys. It should be read as a scope only when the leaf declares `scopes`.
defects.cause: scope shape tested without checking the leaf declares scopes

defects.claim: A condition reads a cleared clearable number as its default, while the form shows it empty
defects.scenario: `{ kind: 'number', name: 'Limit', clearable: true, default: 5 }` (PrefNumber allows a clearable leaf a numeric default: "its default may be too"), held as `undefined` after the person empties the field. `prefValueOrDefault` (leafValue.ts:16) says a clearable leaf holding nothing "is cleared, and shows nothing", so the row draws an empty field. `prefReader`/`prefJudge` read the same path through `unsetValue`, which returns `leaf.default` = 5, so `{ path: 'limit' }` holds and `{ path: 'limit', is: null }` fails while the field visibly holds nothing. `prefJudge` promises to compare "each value as the control over its leaf ... shows it". The same applies to a clearable field of an object or a list entry (`fieldValue`, `entryValue`). Two answers to "what does a leaf holding nothing show"; `unsetValue` should answer `undefined` for a clearable leaf, as `prefValueOrDefault` does.
defects.cause: clearable ignored in the condition reader's absent-value fallback
